subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Should OpenClaw expose this as a local `web_fetch` config surface, a managed-proxy boundary, or a broader cross-tool policy covering `web_fetch`, `web_search`, browser navigation, redirects, caches, and provider fallback?
rationale: This is a public operator-trusted security boundary, and the existing open PRs encode different answers that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve scoped web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while tracking deny/search/proxy coverage explicitly.

options.title: Make proxy policy canonical
options.body: Pause local `web_fetch` config additions and route application-owned egress through the managed proxy policy direction.

options.title: Require cross-tool design
options.body: Hold implementation until maintainers define one policy covering fetch, search, browser, provider fallback, redirects, caches, and plugin HTTP.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while tracking deny/search/proxy coverage explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest web_fetch and guarded-fetch SSRF history across the affected runtime and config paths.
